verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents self-hosting end to end. Sources cover a one-line Docker run, running from a container image, Operator installs on Kubernetes/OpenShift, switching to PostgreSQL, clustering, reverse-proxy setup, health endpoints, and rolling updates. Many independent users report running it themselves for years, clustered, on Docker and on-prem. Some community reports cite heavy memory use and past container pain, but these are resource caveats, not counter-evidence to self-hosting. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license statement in the evidence, and corroboration that a lightweight footprint is achievable.
